Granddaughter loves them and knows her ABC's at 20 months
Great purchase! Loved how soft and durable it was. Perfect gift, exceeded expectations.
The best. Won't hurt your dog and very strong.

I was honestly shocked when this arrived a full day early, the box was pristine, not a single dent. Inside, everything was packed snug in molded cardboard, so zero plastic waste to wrestle with. My toddler ripped it open and immediately locked onto the bright colors and chunky gears. The first thing she did was slap the center button, and the whole thing lit up with this cheerful little tune that got her bouncing. She figured out stacking the gears in about thirty seconds and now won't stop pulling them off just to hear the click. It's sturdy enough that I don't flinch when she drops it, and quiet enough that I'm not losing my mind. Instant hit.
Very durable and cute minty snowball for my power chewer labs.
The practical effects in this are insane. That glowing alien design still holds up, and the synth soundtrack just locks you right into the retro vibe from the first frame.
Lately I've been using a towel again. Its easier to wash and dry then the rubber mat.

This brush is a game-changer for my long-haired cat. It glides through his coat with zero pulling, and he actually purrs during grooming sessions. The size makes it super easy to handle, and it gets all the hidden tangles. Highly recommend.

I'm only giving 2 stars because of how annoying this toy gets. It's so loud and there is no on off or lower volume setting. As soon as the battery is in if the trigger is pulled it goes off extremely loudly. It's a good product maybe for a child old enough to play outside on there own but for my toddler the fact I could not turn it off or adjust the volume made this toy a hell on earth for me. However it does work well and lights up and blasts loudly for the price so if you don't mind the fact it's never ending, then go for it!!!!
Cute, quirky, "this would never happen in real life" romantic short story. this is a good quick read for anyone who still believes in fairy tale endings.
I'd tell any die-hard concert collector to grab this, the sound mix is incredible, and it feels like you're right in the front row. Perfect for weekend watch parties.

The material quality is fine, but they are the thinnest beds I have ever purchased. Luckily we purchased two for the travel crate. The beds we get a Costco are much superior quality at a much less expense. We were specifically attempting to fit a crate for travel NEXT week, otherwise I would have sent them back. Very disappointed..........

I tore through this in two days because the pacing just wouldn't let me go. The way the author weaves work chaos and emotional messiness felt so true to life. I especially appreciated how the heroine's guarded vulnerability slowly cracked open, it made the ending feel earned without being sappy.

I picked these up hoping to round out my utensil drawer without spending a fortune, and they sort of land in that middle zone. The styling is simple and modern, which I appreciate, but in person the satin finish looks a bit flatter than the product photos led me to believe. Weight-wise, they feel noticeably lighter than what I'm used to, fine for casual meals, less satisfying when cutting into something dense. After a couple of weeks of regular use and dishwasher cycles, a few butter knives have developed faint spotting, which surprised me since I baby my kitchen stuff. Not a disaster, and for the price I can't complain too loudly, just wish the everyday feel matched the initial impression.
My kids love all the Monopolies, especially this one. Just wish that the pictures on the properties shown on the board were also pictured on the property cards like with the Marvel Comics Edition.

I picked up this scale mainly for my sourdough baking experiments, and honestly it's been a game changer. The tare function works flawlessly, I can dump flour, water, starter into one bowl and reset to zero between each ingredient without any lag or drift. Measurements are dead accurate down to the gram, and the display is bright enough to read even with a giant mixing bowl on top. I've tested it against my old scale multiple times and this one is spot on every time. The slim profile tucks away easily in a drawer too. For the price, the precision and responsiveness are seriously impressive. If you bake anything that requires exact ratios, this little thing will make your life so much easier.

I expected another hefty Wally Lamb read, but this one hit differently, raw and intimate. The shifting perspectives hooked me harder than his earlier work, and the family dynamics felt uncomfortably real. I planned to pace myself and still burned through it in three nights.

Arrived two days early in a slim, no-waste box. Pulled them out and the color pops way better in person, deep crimson, not flat. First try-on felt snug but not tight. Already got a compliment from my neighbor just unboxing them on the porch.

I'm not a huge F1 fan but was curious about the use of multi-angle features on this disk. Was really expecting an "in your face" in-car driver perspective, with extended racing sequences....disappointed with final product. Very fragmented, difficult to follow, repetitive highlights, in-car clips too short too enjoy, pointless selectable race stats etc. Overall, they blew it! It could have been a great DVD if they had designed it to be a seamless experience for the fan! As it is, consider it a novelty disk, and of interest only to diehard F1 fans...If you want racing action checkout Super Speedway or Driven instead!

Obviously a case of Leigh doing most (if not all of the writing) and riding on the coatails of her husbands name recognition. I am sure this would not have been published without Davids name. It is not very sophisticated writing and Polgara is awful immature for someone hundreds of years old. She acts like a spoiled 16 year old.

I went in expecting a tight, character-driven war drama and got a sluggish, unfocused mess instead. The aerial sequences are fine technically, but they have zero emotional weight because the script never gives you a reason to invest. Scenes just happen without building toward anything meaningful. The pacing is brutal, long stretches of nothing punctuated by action that feels hollow. None of the performances land, and the characters are so thinly written I couldn't tell you a single distinctive trait about anyone on screen. I kept waiting for it to click, for some moment that justified the runtime, but it never came. Honestly, I've seen direct-to-streaming knockoffs with more coherence and heart. A real letdown.
These glasses are a great value. The quality is as expected for the price. They should perform adequately.
This one worked well for me. Good value for what I got. Perfect for everyday use, definitely recommend if you need a reliable option.

Recently bought this knife because its size and shape are comfortable to do many things. The quality is very nice as well. Knowing up front, it was not made in Germany, I am happy with its cost and value. Made in Thailand.
It's a decent peek behind the scenes, but felt too brief and surface-level for the price. Some cool art, just wish there was more meat to it.

Great value this time around! I was really hoping for a bigger size but ended up getting just right. The fit is snug and comfortable without feeling tight. Arrived early and everything looked crisp on photos, nothing crooked at all. The phone number stays clear too, which makes it easy to use. Definitely exceeded what I expected in terms of quality and appearance. Highly recommend!

This is a book that you will want to re-read. It is complex and ambiguous, so it takes time to ponder over clues and come up with theories as to what exactly happened and what it means. I will say that the first novella in the book is a very strong, intriguing start. The second novella describes an alien society. It is probably a bit perplexing on the first read through, but it is still an entertaining read and you will at least get the overall picture. I'd recommend this book to any serious science fiction reader, or any serious reader who likes science fiction occasionally. If you don't like science fiction, you might have a knee jerk reaction to the book just because of its genre. I would recommend Wolfe's "the book of the new sun" first, but this is still a great work that merits a 5 by itself.

Only problem wish I'd read Marquees and Midwife first, as it follows this story. Great fast paced read. Keeps you with your nose in book and enjoying the whole time. If you can read Ameline and Virgil after this though both are wonderful stand alone. Great characters and story lines, enjoy!!!

I grabbed this balaclava for early morning runs when the temp dips into the teens. Overall, it does a solid job keeping my face and head warm without turning into a sweaty mess. The material feels soft against the skin and the breathing vents line up well, so I'm not fighting for air during a hard push. My only real gripe is the nose section, it rides up a bit when I'm moving fast and I end up adjusting it more than I'd like. Also wish the neck dropped a touch lower for tucking into my base layer. Still, for the price, it's a reliable piece of winter gear that I reach for constantly.
A stone fell out after having it for just one week. and I did not wear it everyday. Not worth the trouble of sending it back

This book hit me right in the gut. I'm not usually one for memoirs, but her voice is so raw and unflinching that I forgot I was reading. I'd hand this to anyone craving an honest, messy, deeply human story, especially solo travellers or women who've ever felt lost in the woods or in life. Already bought a copy for my sister.

I have to say I am surprised at how cool these are! I ordered these to put them in my camper as ambiance lighting under the edge of the bed and couches and boy are they much more! I am going to be putting these around the slide out edges and more. Have to order more. I love you can cut them to length you want. Acorn Media has provided the DVD with english subtitles which are helpful not only to people who have hearing impediments but to foreigners (specially when politician explain very quickly intricate schemes, with names of men we know nothing about). The story is very interesting from an historical point of view. It begins with Napoleon III being dismissed and ends some times after the Second World War is over. Politics are not seen from Sirius, but through magnifying glasses: dayly and often cynical calculations, fights against political ennemies or so-called friends. Randolph's every days life is a sort of thrilling gambling. For instance, he resigns his charge, thinking the government will become aware it can't do without him; in case it doesn't Randolph will found a new Tory group, modern, kenner on social issues, and overcome the old Tory party. We see how times are changing: at the beginning of the story, upper classes are extremely conservative, prjudiced with birth, wealth, morals, etc and at the end, one of Jennie's niece, an artist, goes to Russia on her own to see what communism is like. Lady Churchill is a fascinating woman! Clever, brave, ambitious, free, quite different from the other women of her time. With such "political beasts" as his father and mother were, we understand why Winston Churchill (remarkably played by Warren Clark) was so outstanding a stateman. Love stories don't lack in the movie; I found particularly moving the love affair between Jennie and the long-suffering Count Kinsky (embodied by the wonderful Jeremy Brett; if you like him, look at "posthumous Bafta for Jeremy Brett" on facebook).Though many tragic events occur (Randolph illness and demise, wars...), the dialogues, always brilliant, are often amusing: clever, cynical, sparkling with wit. People of the high society are depicted in a satirical way. Everything is beautiful: houses, costumes, music, actors: Lee Remick, Jeremy Brett...I find 361 minutes were hardly enough.

Positives: Great acting performances by Pippi and her penguins. Mostly good by everyone else except Carrey and Lansbury, at times, reverted to their stereotypic past learned phrasings and characterizations. Enough uniquely humorous lines and skits to make the movie a mostly novel laughable experience. So, kudos to the writers for those parts. Negatives: Studios with their crew of writers, directors and producers know that making money takes precedence over creativity so with that thought in mind we have the following too predictable scenes: A stereotypic plot framework of a newly divorced couple with teens. Teens have their own issues as well as navigating/mediating the divorce. Dad, as usual, had his own father family issues growing up. Dad is seen as more in love with his monied vocational interests than the kids. Mom, has a new male friend that ends up to be a boor. Yes, gets booted. At stake is a prize piece of property that is predictably going to be procured by Dad after he re-prioritizes with the help of, guess who, penguins. Dad also wins kids and wife after he re-prioritizes with the help of, guess who, penguins. Penguins, at first, were presented in a clever way but towards the end the writers ran out of ideas and the animals just did the same made-up cute tricks found in most animal movies. In summary, if the movie just had Pipi and the penguins to build around it would have had the potential to be creatively - spot on.
